title: Keep VMware guests' desktop working under Hyprland
head: 089a648052c4
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: QEMU's VMware SVGA II emulation is detected as a VMware hypervisor
leads.consequence: QEMU -vga vmware exports the same 0x15ad:0x0405 display and class 0x030000, so this detector returns success on a QEMU guest. The install leaf enables open-vm-tools units, the scaling leaf rewrites user config, and Hyprland forces software GL. But both Arch units have ConditionVirtualization=vmware; systemd tests the actual VM type, so the QEMU VM cannot start these tools. The current QEMU negative test uses virtio-gpu only and misses this input. Distinguish guest identity from display adapter identity (or scope each action to the property it needs) and test QEMU's -vga vmware explicitly.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus Finding 1 (QEMU -vga vmware); Opus verified QEMU IDs in self-check; published in finding text

leads.summary: Refreshing or reinstalling Hyprland configuration silently undoes the VMware 1x correction
leads.consequence: The one-time leaf/migration edits ~/.config/hypr/monitors.lua, but omarchy-refresh-hyprland copies the shipped auto/2 template over that file, and omarchy-reinstall-configs likewise copies /etc/skel. Neither re-runs the VMware fix; the per-user migration is already marked complete. The next session therefore gets auto scale and GDK_SCALE=2 again, contrary to the new manual's unqualified automatic 1x claim. Ensure config refresh/reset reapplies the VMware-specific default or document the manual step.
leads.triage: verified by coordinator (bin/omarchy-refresh-hyprland:11, omarchy-refresh-config:20-43) and Opus self-check; published as Optional note

leads.summary: Scaling migration breaks symlink-managed monitors.lua instead of updating its target
leads.consequence: For a symlinked ~/.config/hypr/monitors.lua (common with dotfile managers), grep follows the link but GNU sed -i without --follow-symlinks replaces the symlink with a standalone file. The version-controlled target stays auto/2; edits made there later stop reaching Hyprland. Follow symlinks when editing, or explicitly refuse and explain the operation. The test only seeds a regular copied file.
leads.triage: dropped: sed -i on symlinked configs is the repo-wide convention (3 of 22 migration sed -i uses follow symlinks); edge case

leads.summary: Enabled vmtoolsd short-circuits repair of the second required unit
leads.consequence: On an existing VMware guest with vmtoolsd.service enabled but vmware-vmblock-fuse.service disabled or missing, the guard exits 0 before the leaf enables both. The per-user migration is marked complete by omarchy-migrate and the guest never gets the drag-and-drop staging unit from this migration. Check both units (and package presence if it matters), or repair each separately. The is-enabled stub in the test ignores which service was queried.
leads.triage: dropped: edge case (vmtoolsd enabled but vmblock not), low impact

leads.summary: A user-selected named monitor rule is not preserved as an effective 2x/GDK pairing
leads.consequence: A user can retain Omarchy's auto/2 lines while adding a named hl.monitor rule for Virtual-1 at scale 2, as the shipped config explicitly invites. The leaf sees auto and rewrites GDK_SCALE from 2 to 1, but Hyprland selects the later named scale-2 rule for that output. This overrides the user's effective GTK/XWayland pairing and does not actually start that monitor at 1x. Only rewrite untouched templates, or inspect the effective monitor rules and avoid changing GDK_SCALE on customized files.
leads.triage: dropped: edge case with named monitor rule, low impact

leads.summary: An administrator-masked vmtoolsd service blocks every later migration and the update
leads.consequence: systemctl is-enabled returns nonzero for a masked unit, so the migration tries to enable both units anyway; systemctl enable fails for the mask under bash -e. The machine marker and per-user marker stay absent, omarchy-migrate exits before the scaling migration and all later migrations, and omarchy-update stops at its migrate step. On the next run the failure repeats until an admin unmasks a service they may have intentionally disabled. Treat masked as an explicit override or isolate/skip guest-tools failure without blocking unrelated upgrades.
leads.triage: dropped: admin-masked unit edge case; not verified by run on real systemd

leads.summary: Open PR #10707 adds the same VMware package and enables the same units in a second migration
leads.consequence: #10707 is diverged, not stacked. A merge-file result using its own merge base has two run_logged hardware/vmware.sh entries and two open-vm-tools package rows, while vmware.sh and vmware-guest-test.sh have unresolved conflict markers. It additionally brings migration 1790241729.sh, whose VMware path runs omarchy-pkg-add and sudo systemctl enable --now even if this PR's earlier migration and machine marker already completed, causing redundant privileged work for every existing user. If resolving by keeping this PR's leaf, #10707's own test fails because its mock only stubs systemd-detect-virt. Consolidate into one leaf/package row/migration and reconcile tests before both are merged.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus Finding 3; published in More findings

leads.summary: The VMware setup leaf is lost unless install/user/all.sh conflict is resolved against current quattro and #12252
leads.consequence: The current quattro tip adds vm-no-animations.sh adjacent to this PR's fix-vmware-scaling.sh, yielding a conflict marker in install/user/all.sh and a GitHub CONFLICTING state for #11911. Diverged open PR #12252 independently adds fix-vmware-cursor.sh to the same hunk and is also CONFLICTING against its own base. A resolution keeping only one of these three leaf calls silently drops VM animations, 1x startup or cursor recovery on first run, and the respective registration test fails. Keep all three when rebasing; #11912 is stacked on this head and is a dependency, not another conflict.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus Q6 (install/user/all.sh conflict); published in Verified

leads.summary: Check availability of open-vm-tools for ARM64 VMware/Fusion guests before promising universal installer support
leads.consequence: Conditional: on a VMware ARM64 guest exposing the VMware PCI GPU, this hardware leaf tries to install open-vm-tools. Arch's currently published PKGBUILD is x86_64-only and the Arch Linux ARM aarch64 open-vm-tools package lookup returns 404 while aarch64 bash/hyprland return 200. If the Omarchy ARM package repositories also lack a build, an offline installer cannot supply the package and the existing-user migration fails, blocking later migrations. Settle this by checking the ARM ISO mirror contents and a VMware Fusion ARM guest's exact PCI IDs; omit/guard the package or provide an ARM build if unsupported.

limits: No live VMware GPU or guest available: compositor rendering, 0x0 mm measurement, arm64 Fusion PCI identity and ISO mirror inventory require hardware or distribution artifacts; no runtime GPU claim is inferred from synthetic tests. The ARM issue is expressly a hypothesis. Every other issue is tied to pinned source, read-only upstream or sandbox receipts.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** `omarchy-hw-vmware` also matches VirtualBox guests with the default VMSVGA adapter, so the new leaf and migration install and enable `open-vm-tools` there.

### The detector matches VirtualBox's default graphics adapter

It accepts any display device with vendor `0x15ad`. VirtualBox's default controller for Linux guests (VMSVGA) presents VMware's SVGA II IDs (`15ad:0405`, class `0300`), and so does QEMU's `-vga vmware`. **Impact:** there, the install leaf and `migrations/1789452465.sh` add the package and enable its units, with `sudo`. The test's VirtualBox case uses `80ee:beef`, used only by the VBoxVGA/VBoxSVGA controllers, not the Linux default.

**Suggested change:** gate the guest tools on `systemd-detect-virt --vm` returning `vmware` (as #10707 does), keep the SVGA check for the rendering and scale fixes, and add a `15ad:0405` VirtualBox test case.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 089a648)</summary>

Appended to the end of `test/shell.d/vmware-guest-test.sh`:

```bash

# VirtualBox's default graphics controller for Linux guests (VMSVGA) presents
# VMware's SVGA II PCI IDs; 80ee:cafe is VirtualBox's own guest device.
write_pci_devices 0x15ad:0x0405:0x030000 0x80ee:0xcafe:0x088000
run_leaf || fail "the leaf no-ops on a VirtualBox guest"
[[ -s $call_log ]] && fail "the leaf no-ops on a VirtualBox guest" "$(<"$call_log")"
pass "the leaf no-ops on a VirtualBox guest"
```

```
bash test/shell.d/vmware-guest-test.sh
```

Actual output (exit status 1). stdout:

```
ok - the VMware guest tools install during hardware setup
ok - the ISO carries open-vm-tools for offline installs
ok - the leaf installs and enables the guest tools on a VMware guest
ok - the leaf no-ops on other hardware
ok - a failing package install fails the leaf without enabling the units
ok - a migration installs the guest tools on existing installs
ok - the migration installs, enables, and starts the guest tools
ok - the migration no-ops once the marker exists
ok - an installer-provisioned guest is left alone without sudo
ok - the migration no-ops on other hardware
ok - a failing package install leaves the migration pending without a marker
```

stderr:

```
pkg-add open-vm-tools
systemctl enable vmtoolsd.service vmware-vmblock-fuse.service
not ok - the leaf no-ops on a VirtualBox guest
```

The unmodified test file passes on the same tree (exit status 0).

Sources: VirtualBox 7.2.20 `src/VBox/Devices/Graphics/DevVGA.cpp` uses `PCI_VENDOR_ID_VMWARE` and `PCI_DEVICE_ID_VMWARE_SVGA2` when `VMSVGAPciId` is on. `ConsoleImplConfigCommon.cpp` turns that on for `GraphicsControllerType_VMSVGA`, and `Global.cpp` makes VMSVGA the default for Linux guest types, including "Arch Linux (64-bit)". Both Arch units carry `ConditionVirtualization=vmware`, so systemd most likely skips them on VirtualBox (not run).
</details>

<details><summary>More findings</summary>

**Guest-tools half duplicates open #10707.** The first two commits are the head of #11910, which was closed as a duplicate of #10707. Merging #10707 and this PR gives add/add conflicts in `install/hardware/vmware.sh` and `test/shell.d/vmware-guest-test.sh`. The auto-merged files carry the `hardware/vmware.sh` leaf line twice and `open-vm-tools` twice, and both migrations remain. Suggested change: drop the tools install here (`install/hardware/vmware.sh`, its `all.sh` line, the packages entry, `migrations/1789452465.sh` and `vmware-guest-test.sh`), keep `bin/omarchy-hw-vmware` and its test, and build the rendering and scale fix on `quattro` or on #10707.

Excerpt; `<tree>` is the first output line, `018a60c`:

```
$ git fetch https://github.com/omacom/omarchy.git pull/10707/head:pr-10707 pull/11911/head:pr-11911
$ git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only pr-10707 pr-11911
CONFLICT (add/add): Merge conflict in install/hardware/vmware.sh
CONFLICT (add/add): Merge conflict in test/shell.d/vmware-guest-test.sh
$ git show <tree>:install/hardware/all.sh | grep -n vmware
3:run_logged "$OMARCHY_INSTALL/hardware/vmware.sh"
6:run_logged "$OMARCHY_INSTALL/hardware/vmware.sh"
```

**Unverified: Xwayland may not get the variable.** Traced in Hyprland 0.56.2 source, not run on a guest. Xwayland is forked from an event-loop idle callback before the first frame emits `hyprland.start` (`xwayland/Server.cpp`, `render/Renderer.cpp`), so the X server's environment would lack `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE`. Its glamor would then stay on SVGA3D and submit linux-dmabuf buffers through the same import path aquamarine#360 fails, contrary to the PR body's XWayland claim. To settle it on a 3D guest, check `/proc/$(pgrep -x Xwayland)/environ` for the variable and launch one X11 client (for example `GDK_BACKEND=x11 nautilus` with no other Nautilus window open).

**Unverified edge case: the variable can outlive the session.** `autostart.lua` imports the whole environment into the systemd user manager, and uwsm does not unset arbitrary imported names on stop. If the user manager survives a logout (an open SSH session, lingering, or re-login within logind's stop delay), the next Hyprland would start with the variable at parse time and render on software GL. `uwsm finalize LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE` would register it for cleanup.
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified:**
- Hyprland 0.56.2's `hl.env` calls `setenv` in the compositor, and start handlers run in registration order, so the vmware handler runs before autostart's import and shell launch.
- The four new test files fail on the merge-base and pass at the head. Six mutants (swapped requires, parse-time `hl.env`, no class check, no scale guard, marker before install, no `is-enabled` shortcut) are each caught.
- The scaling leaf rewrites only the two shipped lines, is idempotent, and leaves user-chosen scales alone.
- Merged with current `quattro`, the only conflict is `install/user/all.sh` (keep both lines, alongside `vm-no-animations.sh`). The PR tests pass there, and the full shell suite shows the same environmental failures with and without the PR.

**Optional notes:**
- `omarchy-refresh-hyprland` (menu: Update > Config > Hyprland) copies the shipped `monitors.lua` back, restoring `"auto"` and GDK scale 2. The leaf does not run again after that, so `manual/33-monitors.md` could mention the manual step.
- `vmware-scaling-test.sh` checks `[[ -n $migration ]]`, which is always true. `[[ -f $migration ]]` tests that the migration exists.
- The comment in `install/hardware/vmware.sh` that vmtoolsd starts VGAuthService: no such code path was found in open-vm-tools 13.1.0.
</details>
